library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Leung et al. (2023) fitted the same 16-compartment semi-physiological model
separately to tenofovir (TFV, given as tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, TDF) and
to emtricitabine (FTC). The package therefore carries two models that share one
structure and one article:

* `Leung_2023_tenofovir`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Leung_2023_tenofovir"))$description`
* `Leung_2023_emtricitabine`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Leung_2023_emtricitabine"))$description`
* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Leung_2023_tenofovir"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13042> (open access, PMC10725258)
* Supplement: Appendix S1 (Tables S1-S2, Figures S1-S7) and Appendix S2 (the
  two final NONMEM 7.3 control streams, `run15` for FTC and `run17` for TFV).

# Population

The data came from a phase I, open-label, single-dose study in healthy,
premenopausal, HIV-negative women (NCT01330199, University of North Carolina).
Participants took one oral dose of TDF 150, 300 or 600 mg or of FTC 100, 200 or
400 mg. Plasma was sampled intensively over 48 h. Each participant gave one
vaginal, one cervical and one rectal biopsy at 6, 12, 24 or 48 h post-dose.

Twenty-three participants were modelled for each drug. The TFV dataset had 413
observations: 275 in plasma plus 23 TFV and 23 TFV-DP in each tissue. The FTC
dataset had 573. Supplementary Table S1 gives the demographics of the enrolled
arms. The TDF arm (N = 25) had median age 27 years, weight 67.4 kg and BMI
24.1 kg/m^2, and was 64% Caucasian, 32% African American and 4% Asian American.
The FTC arm (N = 24) had median age 22 years, weight 62.8 kg and BMI
22.5 kg/m^2, and was 75% Caucasian, 16.7% African American, 4.2% Asian American
and 4.2% American Indian. The paper tested no covariates because the population
was homogeneous.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Leung_2023_tenofovir")()$population)
```

# Model structure

Figure 1 of the paper and both control streams give the same structure:

* The oral dose sits in `depot`. It empties in parallel into plasma (`central`,
  rate `ka`) and into a seven-stage gut-transit chain (`transit1` to
  `transit7`, rate `ktr` = Kg). The depot therefore loses `ka + ktr`, and only
  the fraction `ka / (ka + ktr)` of the dose reaches plasma.
* Plasma is a two-compartment model (`central`, `peripheral1`).
* The total plasma clearance `cl` (CLtt) leaves plasma in full. The fractions
  `fcl_vagina`, `fcl_cervix` and `fcl_rectum` (Fv, Fe, Fr) of it carry drug
  into the three tissues, and the remainder `1 - Fv - Fe - Fr` is eliminated
  (Equation 1).
* Each tissue holds the parent drug (`vagina`, `cervix`, `rectum`), cleared at
  `cl_<tissue>` (CLttvvtp, CLttve, CLttvr). The fraction `fm_<tissue>` (Fvt,
  Fet, Frt) of that loss forms the phosphorylated anabolite in the same tissue
  (`<tissue>_tfvdp` or `<tissue>_ftctp`), which is cleared at
  `cl_<tissue>_<metab>` (CLvvtp, CLvetp, CLvrtp). The rest is lost in mucosal
  secretions (Equations 2-3).
* The last gut-transit stage moves drug into rectal tissue (`ka_rectum`, Kga)
  and out of the body (`kel_gut`, Kgr). This produces the delayed second rise
  of the rectal concentrations.
* The tissue volumes are fixed to physiological tissue weights at a density of
  1 g/mL: vagina 0.09 L, cervix 0.01 L, rectum 0.17 L. The same volume is used
  for the parent and the metabolite state.

Amounts are in nmol and concentrations in nmol/L. A TDF dose in mg becomes
`mg / 635.52 * 1e6` nmol of TFV (one TFV per TDF, MW 635.52 g/mol). An FTC dose
becomes `mg / 247.24 * 1e6` nmol.

# Virtual cohort and simulation

The cohort reproduces the study design: three dose arms per drug (50%, 100% and
200% of the licensed dose), 100 virtual participants per arm, one dose at time
0, and observations to 48 h. Both models declare seven endpoints, so the
observation rows name the plasma state (`cmt = "central"`) and set `dvid = 1`;
rxode2 then returns every concentration column on every row.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20231201)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231201)

obs_times <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48)
mw <- c(TFV = 635.52, FTC = 247.24)
n_per_arm <- 100L

make_arm <- function(drug, dose_mg, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  amt <- dose_mg / mw[[drug]] * 1e6
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = amt, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
    dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(drug = drug, dose_mg = dose_mg, dose_nmol = amt[1]) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

arms <- data.frame(
  drug = c("TFV", "TFV", "TFV", "FTC", "FTC", "FTC"),
  dose_mg = c(150, 300, 600, 100, 200, 400),
  ref_mg = c(300, 300, 300, 200, 200, 200)
)
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_arm(arms$drug[i], arms$dose_mg[i], (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
})) |>
  mutate(arm = paste(drug, dose_mg, "mg"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 1, "id"]))
```

```{r simulate}
mod_tfv <- readModelDb("Leung_2023_tenofovir")
mod_ftc <- readModelDb("Leung_2023_emtricitabine")

conc_cols <- function(sim, metab) {
  sim |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    rename_with(~ sub(paste0("_", metab, "$"), "_metab", .x))
}

sim_tfv <- rxSolve(mod_tfv, events = filter(events, drug == "TFV"),
                   keep = c("drug", "arm", "dose_mg", "dose_nmol")) |>
  conc_cols("tfvdp")
sim_ftc <- rxSolve(mod_ftc, events = filter(events, drug == "FTC"),
                   keep = c("drug", "arm", "dose_mg", "dose_nmol")) |>
  conc_cols("ftctp")

out_cols <- c("Cc", "Cvagina", "Cvagina_metab", "Ccervix", "Ccervix_metab",
              "Crectum", "Crectum_metab")
sim <- bind_rows(sim_tfv, sim_ftc) |>
  select(id, time, drug, arm, dose_mg, dose_nmol, all_of(out_cols)) |>
  left_join(arms, by = c("drug", "dose_mg"))
```

# Replicate published figures

The model is linear, so the pcVPCs of Figure 3 (and Figures S5-S6), which pool
the three arms after normalising them to the licensed dose, correspond to
dose-normalised simulated concentrations (`C * ref_mg / dose_mg`). The bands
below are the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the individual predictions;
residual error is not added.

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
matrix_labels <- c(
  Cc = "Plasma, parent", Cvagina = "Vaginal tissue, parent",
  Cvagina_metab = "Vaginal tissue, metabolite", Ccervix = "Cervical tissue, parent",
  Ccervix_metab = "Cervical tissue, metabolite", Crectum = "Rectal tissue, parent",
  Crectum_metab = "Rectal tissue, metabolite"
)
# Pre-dose concentrations are zero and cannot be drawn on a log axis.
sim_post <- sim[sim$time > 0, ]
vpc <- sim_post |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(out_cols), names_to = "output", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(conc_norm = conc * ref_mg / dose_mg) |>
  group_by(drug, output, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(conc_norm, 0.05), Q50 = median(conc_norm),
    Q95 = quantile(conc_norm, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    output = factor(matrix_labels[output], levels = matrix_labels),
    drug = factor(drug, levels = c("TFV", "FTC"))
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_grid(output ~ drug, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 48, 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)",
    y = "Dose-normalised concentration (nmol/L)",
    title = "Simulated 5th-50th-95th percentiles, normalised to TDF 300 mg / FTC 200 mg",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 (plasma, vaginal and rectal parent) and Figures S5-S6 (cervix, metabolites) of Leung 2023."
  ) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
```

## Typical values against Figure 3

The table below compares the typical-value profile (random effects set to zero)
with the median of the simulated band in Figure 3, read off the log-scaled
panels by eye. Those readings are approximate, to roughly a factor of 1.5,
so the check catches gross errors such as a wrong dose unit, a misplaced power
of ten or a wrong fraction. It cannot detect a 10% difference.

```{r typical}
typ_events <- bind_rows(
  make_arm("TFV", 300, 0) |> filter(id == 1),
  make_arm("FTC", 200, 0) |> filter(id == 1)
)
typ <- bind_rows(
  rxSolve(zeroRe(mod_tfv), filter(typ_events, drug == "TFV"), keep = "drug") |>
    conc_cols("tfvdp"),
  rxSolve(zeroRe(mod_ftc), filter(typ_events, drug == "FTC"), keep = "drug") |>
    conc_cols("ftctp")
)

# Approximate medians read from Figure 3 (nmol/L, licensed-dose normalised).
fig3 <- tribble(
  ~drug, ~output, ~time, ~figure,
  "TFV", "Cc", 1.5, 600,
  "TFV", "Cc", 48, 35,
  "TFV", "Cvagina", 6, 85,
  "TFV", "Cvagina", 24, 50,
  "TFV", "Cvagina", 48, 20,
  "TFV", "Crectum", 6, 60,
  "TFV", "Crectum", 24, 160,
  "TFV", "Crectum", 48, 1500,
  "FTC", "Cc", 2, 5000,
  "FTC", "Cc", 48, 80,
  "FTC", "Cvagina", 6, 4500,
  "FTC", "Cvagina", 24, 1300,
  "FTC", "Cvagina", 48, 350,
  "FTC", "Crectum", 6, 6000,
  "FTC", "Crectum", 24, 5000,
  "FTC", "Crectum", 48, 9500
)
typ_cmp <- typ |>
  select(drug, time, all_of(out_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(out_cols), names_to = "output", values_to = "model") |>
  inner_join(fig3, by = c("drug", "output", "time")) |>
  mutate(ratio = model / figure)

typ_cmp |>
  mutate(output = matrix_labels[output], model = signif(model, 3), ratio = round(ratio, 2)) |>
  rename(
    Drug = drug, Output = output, "Time (h)" = time,
    "Model typical value (nmol/L)" = model, "Figure 3 median, approx. (nmol/L)" = figure,
    "Model / figure" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Every point is within a factor of 2 of the figure. The ratios are not tight,
# because the figure readings are approximate, but a dose-unit or power-of-ten
# error would move them by 10-fold or more.
stopifnot(all(typ_cmp$ratio > 0.5 & typ_cmp$ratio < 2))
```

The lowest ratio is FTC in rectal tissue at 24 h, at about 0.54. The typical
rectal FTC profile falls to a trough near 24 h and then climbs again as the
gut-transit chain delivers unabsorbed drug (36 h: about 5700 nmol/L; 48 h:
about 12000 nmol/L). The figure's band for that time spans the 18-36 h bin, so
it averages over the trough and the start of the climb, and it sits above the
24 h trough value. The observed median line in the same panel dips to about
2500 nmol/L at 24 h, close to the model's typical value.

## Mass balance of the absorbed fraction

The depot empties into plasma and into the gut-transit chain in parallel. So
the plasma exposure of a typical subject is
`AUC = dose * ka / (ka + ktr) / CLtt`, and the rest of the dose goes down the
gut. The simulated plasma AUC (trapezoids on a fine grid to 2000 h) must match
this closed form. Both sides use the same typical parameters, so the
tolerance is tight.

```{r mass-balance}
fine <- c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.05), seq(48.5, 2000, by = 0.5))

auc_mass_balance <- function(mod, dose_nmol) {
  m <- mod()
  ka <- exp(m$theta[["lka"]])
  ktr <- exp(m$theta[["lktr"]])
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = c(0, fine), amt = c(dose_nmol, rep(0, length(fine))),
    evid = c(1L, rep(0L, length(fine))),
    cmt = c("depot", rep("central", length(fine))),
    dvid = c(NA_integer_, rep(1L, length(fine)))
  )
  s <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(zeroRe(m), ev))
  c(
    simulated = sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2),
    closed_form = dose_nmol * ka / (ka + ktr) / exp(m$theta[["lcl"]]),
    fraction_to_plasma = ka / (ka + ktr)
  )
}
auc_tab <- as.data.frame(rbind(
  TFV = auc_mass_balance(mod_tfv, 300 / mw[["TFV"]] * 1e6),
  FTC = auc_mass_balance(mod_ftc, 200 / mw[["FTC"]] * 1e6)
))
knitr::kable(signif(auc_tab, 4), caption = "Typical plasma AUC0-inf (nmol*h/L) and fraction of the dose absorbed into plasma.")
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_tab$simulated / auc_tab$closed_form - 1) < 0.005))
```

# PKNCA validation

Plasma NCA per drug and dose arm. The paper reports no NCA values, so there is
no published table to compare against. The check is that exposure is
dose-proportional (the model is linear) and that the median AUC matches the
closed form above.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, arm) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, arm, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, arm, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(arm, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  left_join(distinct(events, arm, drug, dose_mg), by = "arm") |>
  arrange(desc(drug), dose_mg) |>
  mutate(auc_per_mg = aucinf.obs / dose_mg)

nca_summary |>
  mutate(across(c(cmax, aucinf.obs, half.life, auc_per_mg), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  select(arm, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life, auc_per_mg) |>
  rename(
    Arm = arm, "Cmax (nmol/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (nmol*h/L)" = aucinf.obs, "Half-life (h)" = half.life,
    "AUC0-inf per mg" = auc_per_mg
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated plasma NCA by arm (100 participants per arm).")

# Dose proportionality: within each drug the AUC per mg differs between arms
# only by sampling noise, because the model is linear.
prop_check <- nca_summary |>
  group_by(drug) |>
  summarise(spread = max(auc_per_mg) / min(auc_per_mg))
stopifnot(all(prop_check$spread < 1.3))

# The terminal half-life over 48 h reflects the distribution phase, so it is
# reported, not asserted.
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **FTC CLttvvtp.** Table 1 prints the FTC value as `0101`, with the decimal
  point lost. The maintainers read it as 0.0101 L/h. The control-stream
  initial estimate is 0.0123 with an upper bound of 1, which rules out 1.01,
  and 0.101 fails against Figure 3e. With 0.0101 the typical vaginal FTC concentration is about 4500
  nmol/L at 6 h and 1400 nmol/L at 24 h, as in the figure. With 0.101 it would
  be about 720 and 48 nmol/L.
* **Dose units.** The paper converted concentrations to nmol/L but does not say
  how the doses were converted. The model takes doses in nmol: TDF mg / 635.52
  x 1e6 (one tenofovir per TDF molecule) and FTC mg / 247.24 x 1e6. The plasma
  peaks this gives (about 580 nmol/L TFV and 5100 nmol/L FTC at the licensed
  doses) match Figure 3a/3d. All volumes and clearances are apparent (oral)
  values. Bioavailability is not separated from them, and the
  `ka / (ka + ktr)` split decides how much of the dose reaches plasma.
* **Fixed parameters.** Table 1 marks FTC Fet, Kga and Kgr and TFV Frt and Kgr
  as fixed. TFV Fr is also encoded as fixed: Table 1 does not mark it, but the
  control stream has `(0.00007 FIX)`, which equals the Table 1 value of
  7.00e-5. The six tissue volumes are fixed in both models (Methods, Results).
* **Residual-error row label.** The last sigma row of Table 1 is printed as
  "Metabolite in plasma". The paper modelled no plasma metabolite. In both
  control streams the seventh epsilon applies to the rectal metabolite
  (compartment 9), so the row is the rectal metabolite's error.
* **Residual-error correlations not carried.** Each tissue has a parent and
  metabolite residual-error covariance (`$SIGMA BLOCK(2)`; the off-diagonal
  values are shown in brackets in Table 1). The nlmixr2 error model cannot
  express a correlation between the residuals of two endpoints. The
  proportional SDs are kept and the correlations are dropped. This affects
  only joint simulation of the observed parent and metabolite in the same
  biopsy, not the individual predictions.
* **IIV scale.** Table 1 reports IIV as %CV. The control streams start every
  omega at 0.1, which does not show which convention produced the %CV. The
  maintainers used the exact log-normal conversion
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`, the package's convention. For the wide rows
  (CLvetp 172% and 164.9%, CLvvtp 97.6%) the alternative `omega^2 = CV^2` would
  give variances about 2.1-2.2 and 1.4 times larger.
* **TFV Vc-CLtt correlation of 100%.** Table 1 reports the TFV Vc-CLtt
  off-diagonal as a 100% correlation. It is encoded as a full-correlation
  block, so CLtt and Vc share one random effect scaled by their SDs. rxode2
  simulates it without error.
* **Residual SD.** The %CV of each proportional residual error is taken as
  100 x SD, so `propSd` is the %CV / 100. FTC rectal parent has a printed 1.51%,
  which is unusually small; it is kept as published.
* **No erratum** for this article was found on the publisher page or in
  PubMed (checked 2026-11-07).
